cards.front: What fills GPU memory when serving an LLM?
cards.back: The model weights, which are fixed, and the KV cache, which grows with every token of every active request.
weights ≈ parameters × bytes per parameter. An 8B model is about 16 GB in BF16 and 8 GB in FP8, before any KV cache.
No. A 120B MoE with about 12B active parameters needs memory for 120B and compute for about 12B. MoE saves compute per token, not memory.
Keeps the keys and values of earlier tokens so each new token costs one step instead of reprocessing the whole prefix. The price is memory that grows with every token.
2 × layers × KV heads × head dim × bytes per value. For Llama 3.1 8B in FP16 that is 128 KiB per token, so an 8,000-token conversation holds about 1 GiB.
Like virtual memory: a block table maps each sequence to the blocks it owns, so nobody reserves the longest possible sequence and more requests fit at once.
Requests that share a prefix, such as a common system prompt, reuse its KV blocks instead of computing them again.
Tensor splits every layer across GPUs and needs heavy GPU-to-GPU traffic, so keep it in one node. Pipeline puts different layers on different GPUs, with less traffic but idle stages.

cards.front: When to add replicas instead of tensor parallelism
cards.back: Use tensor parallelism when the model doesn't fit on one GPU, and replicas when it fits but you need more throughput.
The prompt processing (prefill) time. It grows with prompt length and is helped by prefix caching and shorter prompts.
A small draft model proposes tokens and the big model checks several at once, which speeds up memory-bound decoding for one user.

quiz.q: A server runs out of memory as more users join, though the model loads fine. What is the likely cause?
quiz.why: Each active request's KV cache grows with its tokens; fix it with a paged or 8-bit KV cache, a lower max sequence length or more GPUs.

quiz.q: Single-user tokens per second are slow. Which lever does NOT target it?
quiz.why: Replicas add throughput across users; per-user decoding is memory-bound and helped by speculative decoding, quantization and tensor parallelism.

quiz.q: Roughly how much KV cache do 40 conversations of 8,000 tokens need on Llama 3.1 8B in FP16?
quiz.why: At 128 KiB per token each conversation holds about 1 GiB, so 40 of them hold more than the model's own 16 GB of weights.

quiz.q: Which metric does prefix caching mainly improve?
quiz.why: TTFT is prefill time, and prefix caching skips recomputing a shared prompt prefix.

quiz.q: A 120B model in FP8 runs on four 80 GB GPUs with tensor parallelism. About how much is left for the KV cache?
quiz.why: 320 GB total minus about 120 GB of FP8 weights leaves about 200 GB.

quiz.q: Quality dropped right after an engine upgrade with FP8. What do you do first?
choices: Rerun the eval set and roll back if needed
quiz.why: Quantization or engine changes can move quality, so rerun the eval set and roll back.

quiz.q: Which parallelism suits a mixture-of-experts model but risks uneven load?
quiz.why: Expert parallelism places experts on different GPUs; popular experts load some GPUs more than others.
